interactions.title: First journal: learning words and growing into houses
lines: DM: And you come out against the far wall, the north wall. There's not an exit there. But what there is is something that's almost like a window, like a 2 foot by 2 foot cutout in the wall. And you're looking through about, I don't know, 3 feet of stone wall, and on the other side of it, flush against it, as if it's just a recessed back, but you get this distinct impression of being a window, is a two-foot square of elaborately inscribed iron wall, with… just covered in runes and arcane markings that you can't decipher. And right next to it, so you've dodged under this big pipe to come out next to this window thing, there is a chair and a writing desk with a journal on top of it.
Tarek: Let's have a look at that.

DM: They seem to be notes, and they are numbered, by date. With dates that don't… exactly makes sense, or at least it's a little challenging to do the translation from Drankorian in your head, but… And… There's probably about 30 pages or so filled on a small, maybe 4 inch by 6 inch notebook, that comprises 15 or 20 entries, the dates of which seem to be, you know, some of them are really close back to back, and some of them are farther apart. There's no discernible pattern, to what that looks like. Though the last one is a very long time ago now, so it was… I mean, 700-some years ago. And it seems to be a transcription of, like, a monologue? And… ahhh!

DM: And it goes something like this. So it's in quotes, and it says… "When I get here, I do not know anyone. But there is a teacher who is very patient with me. He's teaching me about words. He's teaching me that words have an order. Words have a before and an after. He says that words are a game to play, because of course there is no such thing as before, and no such thing as after, except that words make it so. He says that if I am to play games with the dreamers, I am learning about the order of words." That's the first entry, and someone's… scrawled notes to themselves below it, saying, like, child? Question mark? Timeline? Question mark?

DM: The next entry continues, he says, or with another quote, he says: "I am learning about the order of words. My teacher teaches me about eating and drinking. About sunset and stars. About beginnings and endings. He teaches me about the danger of cold iron and the fearfulness of the dreamers. He teaches me that words are letters, and brings me books, and I am reading them. He teaches me about trees, and roots, and leaves, and mushrooms, and houses, and hedges, and roads, and doors." And there's a note below it that says, "This list continues in this vein for some time."

DM: The next entry is a little while later. It says… "This world is strange and scary. I am alone without the teacher. His evening is beginning, he tells me. He comes back, he tells me. He is not coming back. He is forgetting me. I'm not going to him. I'm going past his house. I'm going on and on and on and on." And there's another note below it that says, "This continues for some time." You…

DM: The entries go on in this vein, sort of page after page, this odd jumble of things being learned. A sense of abandonment and fear. An almost childish… pride in not needing a teacher anymore. Though, oddly, it's all written in the present tense.

DM: Until finally, on the last entry, it says, "I am grown. The world is very big. I'm tall. I stretch out. My hands are under a very bright and changing sky. My legs are reaching between trees and roots and leaves and mushrooms and becoming houses." And that's the last entry in that.
